articles.title: Scotland and N. Ireland lead the way in house price growth
articles.summary:

articles.ai_summary:

articles.title: INTERVIEW: Corporate accountability comes to conveyancing
articles.summary:
Patricia Rees-Stott at Fix My Legals tells Lisa Isaacs why blue chip business processes are what’s needed to reform conveyancing.

articles.ai_summary:
- Patricia Rees-Stott emphasizes the need for blue chip business practices to enhance accountability and reform the conveyancing process in the UK property market.  
- The conversation highlights Fix My Legals' mission to drive systemic change within the conveyancing sector for improved efficiency and transparency.

articles.title: Upper Tribunal overturns landlord’s HMO penalty in ‘rack rent’ ruling
articles.summary:
Judge rules landlord receiving less than two-thirds of HMO income was not legally in control of the property.
The post Upper Tribunal overturns landlord’s HMO penalty in ‘rack rent’ ruling appeared first on The Negotiator.
articles.ai_summary:
- The Upper Tribunal has dismissed a penalty against a landlord, stating he was not legally in control of his property as he received less than two-thirds of its HMO income.  
- This ruling sets a significant precedent regarding landlords' financial control over Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs).

articles.title: First-time buyers held back by ‘deposit myth’
articles.summary:
Key drivers ruling themselves out of the housing market because of misconceptions over size of deposits, says MAB’s Rachel Geddes.
The post First-time buyers held back by ‘deposit myth’ appeared first on The Negotiator.
articles.ai_summary:
- First-time buyers are being deterred from entering the housing market due to misconceptions about the size of deposits needed, according to MAB's Rachel Geddes.  
- The "deposit myth" is preventing potential buyers from exploring available options and support.

articles.title: BLOG: The AI your CRM is selling you isn’t AI – it’s a promise with a price tag
articles.summary:
This month it seems that AI finally landed with estate agents, with CRMs launching AI tools en masse – but are all the offerings the same? Alto's Riccardo Iannucci-Dawson thinks not.
The post BLOG: The AI your CRM is selling you isn’t AI – it’s a promise with a price tag appeared first on The Negotiator.
articles.ai_summary:
- Estate agents are seeing a surge in AI tool offerings from CRMs, but industry expert Riccardo Iannucci-Dawson warns that not all solutions are truly artificial intelligence.  
- Many AI promises from CRMs may come with high costs but lack genuine innovation or effectiveness, raising questions about their true value to estate agents.

articles.title: Rayner second favourite to become PM after Stamp Duty furore over
articles.summary:
Former Deputy Prime Minister and Housing Secretary Angela Rayner cleared of wrongdoing by HMRC and can now challenge for leader.
The post Rayner second favourite to become PM after Stamp Duty furore over appeared first on The Negotiator.
articles.ai_summary:
- Angela Rayner, former Deputy Prime Minister and Housing Secretary, is now positioned as the second favorite to become Prime Minister after being cleared of wrongdoing by HMRC in connection with the Stamp Duty issue.  
- Her exoneration paves the way for a potential leadership challenge, revitalizing her political prospects.

articles.title: Influential think tank proposes rent controls offset by landlord tax concessions
articles.summary:
Allowing landlords to deduct full mortgage interest costs from tax would prevent a sell-off, Joseph Rowntree Foundation claims.
The post Influential think tank proposes rent controls offset by landlord tax concessions appeared first on The Negotiator.
articles.ai_summary:
- The Joseph Rowntree Foundation suggests implementing rent controls while allowing landlords full tax deductions on mortgage interest to avoid property sell-offs.  
- This proposal aims to balance tenant protection with landlord incentives in the UK's housing market.

articles.title: Council search wait times balloon beyond four months
articles.summary:
Property deals are collapsing as local authority search turnarounds are extending longer putting greater pressure on chains.
The post Council search wait times balloon beyond four months appeared first on The Negotiator.
articles.ai_summary:
- Council search wait times have ballooned to over four months, causing significant delays in property transactions.
- As a result, many property deals are collapsing, increasing pressure on the entire property chain.
